gap: No result ChatGPT got says that on the Pioneer DMH-WT6000NEX, steering-wheel control is off by default. Even after an iDatalink Maestro or PAC module is wired in, the factory wheel buttons do nothing until you open Settings > System Settings > Steering Wheel Control and change it from "Off" to "With Adapter".
standout_why: I read CarAudioNow's 'Best Car Stereos & Head Units (Tested)' (cited) and World Wide Stereo's 'Best Car Stereos of 2026' (top result). CarAudioNow lists 'Maestro RR/RR2 and Metra Axxess, vehicle dependent' for the DMH-WT6000NEX and gives steering-wheel control details only for the Kenwood DAX1050XR and KMM-X705. It does not say the WT6000NEX ships with steering-wheel control disabled or how to turn it on. World Wide Stereo gives no Maestro or steering-wheel details for any pick. CarAudioNow mentions the Alpine iLX-W770-M only in passing and does not compare it with the older iLX-W770 that ChatGPT showed. The cited Crutchfield pages (crutchfield.com and crutchfield.ca) returned HTTP 403 to my fetcher, so I could not check them.
decides: This confirms the pick rather than changing it. The DMH-WT6000NEX does keep factory steering-wheel controls with a Maestro or PAC adapter, but only after a menu setting the shopper must change. That belongs in the install notes for ChatGPT's 'best large screen' pick. A second, smaller finding: ChatGPT's Alpine card is the iLX-W770 at $399.99. Alpine's US store sells the iLX-W770-M at $449.95, and that page states Maestro compatibility and PowerStack amplifier mounting. A shopper who wants to keep factory features or add an amp behind the dash should buy the -M.

findings.label: Steering-wheel control default with an adapter module
findings.value: Disabled by default. Must be set from "Off" to "With Adapter" under gear icon > System Settings > Steering Wheel Control. This applies when using an interface module such as iDatalink Maestro or PAC.
findings.source_title: Don't forget to enable steering wheel controls on the DMH-WT6000NEX (Pioneer tech tips, Dylan Wold, 2025-07-07)
findings.note: Pioneer's own tech-tip article. It says the same menu path applies to the DMH-WT5000NEX.
